events.title: The death of Pope St. Pius X
events.shortBlurb: Broken-hearted at the coming of the Great War he could not stop, Pius X died in its first weeks, offering his life for the peace of the world…
body: In the summer of 1914 Giuseppe Sarto was in his eightieth year and the eleventh of his pontificate. The lamps were going out across Europe: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July, Germany on Russia on 1 August and on France on 3 August, and Britain answered on 4 August, the eleventh anniversary of his election. The news fell upon the old pope like a sentence.

He sickened on the feast of the Assumption, 15 August, and in the early hours of 20 August 1914 he died of heart failure at the Vatican, whispering, it was reported, that he gladly offered his life for the end of the war. By his will his body was left untouched by the embalmers' knives and laid in a simple tomb in the crypt of St. Peter's.

The cardinals who gathered in his stead chose Giacomo della Chiesa, Benedict XV, whose whole pontificate was a plea for the peace his predecessor had not lived to see. Pius X was beatified in 1951 and canonized by Pius XII on 29 May 1954, the first pope so honoured since Pius V.

sources.text: Vatican biography of Pope St. Pius X (vatican.va)
